chunks: Ali ibn Isma'il al-Mithamī narrated from Ḥammād from 'Abd Allāh ibn al-Mughīrah from Ibn Sīnān from Abū 'Abd Allāh (peace be upon him): Regarding

a man who divorced his wife, then he died while she was in her waiting period, that she inherits him and observes the waiting period of the one who died, her husband. And if she died while she was in the waiting period, then he inherits her. And each of them inherits from the blood-money (diyah) of the other, if killed, provided that one did not kill the other.

key_terms.عِدَّة: Waiting period (Iddah) after death or divorce

ai.seo_question: What are the inheritance and waiting period rules for a divorced couple if one spouse dies before the divorce is finalized?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq clarifies the legal status of a revocable divorce (talaq raj'i) at the moment of death, establishing that the marital bond remains intact for inheritance and 'iddah purposes. It further extends this principle to the mutual inheritance of blood-money (diyah), highlighting the continuity of financial rights even in the transition from life to death, provided there is no homicide. This ruling underscores the Shia jurisprudential view that death does not automatically dissolve the marital tie if the divorce was not yet finalized by the expiration of the waiting period.
